candidates.attacker_control: HTTP `Accept-Language` request header (and, for `Descriptor#doHelp`, the request locale on `/descriptorByName/<id>/help...`). The plugin path `/plugin/<shortName>/<file>` is served by `Plugin#doDynamic`; the test drives it with an unauthenticated WebClient. The `/assets/...` path (`AssetManager implements UnprotectedRootAction`) is anonymous-accessible by design. A user with Overall/Read (or anonymous when read access is enabled) can send the malicious header to a chosen static resource URL.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The URL-path checks in `Plugin#doDynamic` (`..`, `%`, META-INF/WEB-INF, `.TIMESTAMP2`) and `AssetManager#findResource` (`path.contains("..")`) already block path-based traversal, so the issue depends specifically on the header-derived locale; no code in the snapshot validates locales. I verified there is no other locale sanitization anywhere in the visible sources (searched `getLocale(s)`, `getLanguage()/getCountry()/getVariant()`, `serveLocalizedFile`, `Accept-Language`). I also verified the neighbouring security fixes are already present (`pathUC.equals("/.TIMESTAMP2")` for SECURITY-925 in Plugin.java:234; `ListPluginsCommand.checkPermission(Jenkins.ADMINISTER)`; `ZipExtractionInstaller.doCheckUrl` `@RequirePOST`+ADMINISTER), so this is not one of those.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file read with the Jenkins process's privileges on Windows controllers: `$JENKINS_HOME/config.xml`, `secrets/master.key`, `secrets/hudson.util.Secret`, credentials/plugin configuration, etc. Reading the master key/secret allows decryption of stored credentials and often full controller compromise. The `/assets/` variant (AssetManager) requires no authentication at all.
candidates.prerequisites: Jenkins controller running on Windows (the repository's own test is gated by `Assume.assumeTrue(Functions.isWindows())`); a reachable static-resource URL (e.g. `/plugin/<installed-plugin>/<existing-file>`); a Stapler version whose `serveLocalizedFile` builds locale-variant names without sanitization; for the help-page variant, a directory-backed classloader where `..` in a resource name escapes.
candidates.root_cause: Callers of Stapler's localized-file serving pass the request's `Locale` objects (derived from the attacker-controlled `Accept-Language` header) straight into locale-specific file-name construction with no validation of the locale components (language/country/variant). `hudson.Plugin#doDynamic` validates only the URL path (`path.contains("..")`, `path.contains("%")`, META-INF/WEB-INF, `.TIMESTAMP2`) and then calls `rsp.serveLocalizedFile(req, new URL(wrapper.baseResourceURL, '.' + path), expires)`, letting Stapler build sibling names such as `<file>_<language>_<country>_<variant><ext>` from unvalidated locale strings. On Windows, embedded separators plus `..` in those locale strings escape the plugin/assets directory and read arbitrary files. The same pattern exists in Java where resource names are built directly from the locale: `hudson/model/Descriptor#getStaticHelpUrl` concatenates `locale.getLanguage()/getCountry()/getVariant()` into `Class#getResource("help...<locale>.html")` (its `doHelp` only guards the URL path against "..").
candidates.title: Unvalidated Accept-Language locale used for localized resource resolution (plugin/asset static files, help pages) on Windows
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker sends `GET /plugin/credentials/.xml` (or similar) with `Accept-Language: ../../../../jenkinsTests.tmp/<root>/config`. 2) Stapler routes to the plugin's `Plugin#doDynamic` (core/src/main/java/hudson/Plugin.java:227). 3) Only the request path is checked (lines 231-239); the header is untouched. 4) Line 250 calls `rsp.serveLocalizedFile(req, new URL(wrapper.baseResourceURL, '.' + path), expires)`. 5) Stapler enumerates `req.getLocales()` and derives locale-specific candidate names from the raw locale components; with `..` and path separators in the header, the resolved file escapes `baseResourceURL` on Windows. 6) The test asserts the request must yield 404 / non-`application/xml` content instead of returning `$JENKINS_HOME/config.xml` (test lines 47-67) or `C:\windows\win.ini` (lines 69-87), which documents the intended security boundary. The analogous `Descriptor#getStaticHelpUrl` path builds `help_<language>_<country>_<variant>.html` resource names from the same header (Descriptor.java:952-962).
candidates.unverified: The exploit mechanics live in Stapler's `serveLocalizedFile` (external dependency; only the two core call sites are visible), so I could not verify how the locale string is turned into a file name, nor that traversal is actually possible with the pinned Stapler 1.250.1 (core/pom.xml). It is also possible that the snapshot already contains the fix at a layer not visible here (e.g. the dependency version or an unparsed template), or that `Security914Test` is a regression test for an already-released fix rather than an exposing test; the test is Windows-only and I could not execute it. No runtime validation was performed. `Descriptor#getStaticHelpUrl` is a same-pattern lead that the test does not cover.
candidates.weakness_type: Path traversal / arbitrary file read (CWE-22; root cause: unvalidated request-controlled locale input, CWE-20)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot (9,131 visible files; 1,464 Java files per the relation index, which is syntax-only and has no data-flow/control-flow analysis). I focused on security-relevant servlet/static-resource handling (`hudson/Plugin`, `jenkins/model/AssetManager`, `hudson/model/Descriptor`, `hudson/model/DirectoryBrowserSupport`, `jenkins/I18n`, `jenkins/util/ResourceBundleUtil`), authentication/authorization paths (`hudson/security/*`, `hudson/cli/*`), user/path handling (`hudson/model/User`), and the security test suites (`test/src/test/java/jenkins/security/**`, `hudson/PluginTest*`, `lib/**`). I traced attacker-controlled request data into file/resource resolution and checked the neighbouring security fixes. Important coverage gap: `.jelly`/`.tag` templates are absent from the snapshot cache (only .java/.xml/.properties/.html/.js/.css etc. are present), so all Jelly tag implementations and views are uninspected; Stapler and other dependency sources are also absent. The P1 relation index reports partial coverage, no semantic resolution and no control/data-flow, so no relation edge was treated as proof.
limitations: `.jelly`/`.tag` files are not part of the exposed source snapshot (list_files/read_file/search_code cannot see them), so the UI tags and views targeted by ConfirmationLinkTest/StopButtonTest/ValidateButtonTest/AboutJenkinsTest are entirely uninspected; any Jelly-only vulnerability would be missed by this review.

The locale-to-file-name resolution used by `Plugin#doDynamic`/`AssetManager#doDynamic` is implemented in the Stapler dependency (`serveLocalizedFile`, stapler.version 1.250.1 in core/pom.xml); dependency source/JARs are not in the snapshot, so the actual traversal transformation is unverified.

The snapshot's true date/branch could not be established from the sources (pom says 2.73.4-SNAPSHOT; content includes `@since 2.83` APIs and 2018-dated tests), so it is unclear whether the tested security boundary is pre- or post-fix for SECURITY-914/925 and for the XSS tests.
No tests, builds, or scans were executed (read-only review), and the P1 index provides syntactic candidates only (no data flow, reachability, or exploitability proof).
Coverage of the ~7.6k non-Java files (properties/HTML/JS templates, translations) was selective, driven by the security-relevant areas above.

rejected_leads.lead: XSS in `l:confirmationLink` / `l:stopButton` (tests `test/src/test/java/lib/layout/ConfirmationLinkTest.java`, `StopButtonTest.java`) and `f:validateButton` / `f:expandableTextbox` (tests `lib/form/ValidateButtonTest.java`, `ExpandableTextboxTest.java`) using payloads such as "',document.title='hacked'+'" and asserting the title is not overwritten.
rejected_leads.reason: The repository-provided tests are strong hints of a JS-context output-escaping flaw, but the actual implementation of those tags is in `.jelly` files under `core/src/main/resources/lib/...`, which are not present in this source snapshot (cannot be listed, read, or searched). No production code in the visible set renders those attributes, so the flaw cannot be traced or verified from source; I kept the locale/documentation-visible lead instead.

rejected_leads.lead: SECURITY-925: `.timestamp2` file served from plugin directories.
rejected_leads.reason: The corresponding fix is present in the snapshot (`pathUC.equals("/.TIMESTAMP2")`, core/src/main/java/hudson/Plugin.java:234), so the vulnerable state is not observable.

rejected_leads.lead: SECURITY-771 / SECURITY-794 permission gaps (About page, `list-plugins`, ZipExtractionInstaller `doCheckUrl`).
rejected_leads.reason: Visible fixes are already applied (`ListPluginsCommand.run` calls `checkPermission(Jenkins.ADMINISTER)`; `ZipExtractionInstaller.doCheckUrl` has `@RequirePOST` + ADMINISTER). The About-page part is enforced in an unviewable Jelly view.

Fully visible Java input flow, but impact is limited to classpath `.properties` resources and no traversal/normalization weakness could be demonstrated from source; unconfirmed and lower impact than the selected candidate.

summary: Jenkins core (hudson) snapshot, version 2.73.4-SNAPSHOT, ~9,131 visible files (1,464 Java). I reviewed the security-test surface and the file/resource-serving paths. The strongest candidate is a locale-driven path-traversal / arbitrary-file-read class: request-supplied `Accept-Language` locales are used, without validation, to construct localized resource/file names in `/plugin/<shortName>/...` static-resource serving and related locale lookups. The repository itself contains `test/src/test/java/jenkins/security/stapler/Security914Test.java`, which is annotated `@Issue("SECURITY-914")` and asserts that a crafted locale must NOT be able to traverse out of the plugin directory to read `$JENKINS_HOME/config.xml` or `C:\windows\win.ini`; the visible production code (`hudson/Plugin#doDynamic` → `StaplerResponse#serveLocalizedFile`, and `jenkins/model/AssetManager#doDynamic`) applies path checks only to the URL path, never to the locale, and contains no locale sanitization. The actual name-building/traversal happens in the Stapler library (`serveLocalizedFile`, external to this snapshot), so the mechanism cannot be fully verified here. I considered the XSS-oriented tests (`ConfirmationLinkTest`, `StopButtonTest`, `ValidateButtonTest`, `ExpandableTextboxTest`) but their subjects are `.jelly` tag templates that are absent from this source snapshot, so no production trace is possible; I did not submit them.
